findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization uses && instead of ||
findings.body: The permission check is `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be BOTH an admin and an owner of the booking's team. The variable is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner`, so the intent is clearly OR. As written, a team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not flagged admin) is denied the ability to add guests with a FORBIDDEN error, even though the surrounding UI exposes the action to them (e.g. `booking.isUserTeamAdminOrOwner` elsewhere in the codebase treats admin OR owner as authorized). Change `&&` to `||`.

findings.title: Guest email blacklist is bypassed via letter casing
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built by lowercasing each entry of `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (line 71), but the membership test `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw, un-normalized guest email. A guest email like `Blocked@Example.com` will not match the lowercased `blocked@example.com` entry and will be added anyway, defeating the purpose of the env-var blacklist (which exists to stop unwanted guests from being invited/leaking the meeting link). The guest email must be lowercased before comparison.

findings.title: Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendee records
findings.body: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compares emails with strict equality. Emails are routinely written with different casing (e.g. a user typing `John@Mail.com` when the attendee was stored as `john@mail.com`), so a guest that already exists on the booking will pass the filter and be inserted a second time via `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows. These duplicates then receive duplicate emails and appear twice in the booking UI. Both sides should be compared case-insensitively (as the blacklist comparison a few lines up already assumes).

findings.title: EventManager is constructed with the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is used to push the new guests onto the organizer's calendar event, but the EventManager is built from `ctx.user` (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, ... })`). When the caller is an attendee or a team admin rather than the booking's organizer, their credentials do not include the calendar integration that owns the booking's destination calendar, so the calendar event will not be updated (or may target the wrong calendar). The organizer's user record is already fetched (with credentials included in the booking query at line 35-40); the EventManager should be built from `booking.user`, matching how other booking mutations handle this.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails is passed the raw guests list instead of the filtered uniqueGuests
findings.body: The email fan-out is called as `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, using the original request input rather than `uniqueGuests` (the list after removing already-present and blacklisted emails). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts line 541) the decision of whether an attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` is based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`, so stale/blacklisted emails influence which email template existing attendees receive. Additionally that `includes` check is case-sensitive, so a new guest whose email casing differs from the stored attendee row will get the 'guests added' notice instead of the full 'scheduled' email containing their booking details. Pass `uniqueGuests` and compare case-insensitively.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails metadata
findings.body: Every other notification helper in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts `eventTypeMetadata` and short-circuits on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, honoring the organizer's 'disable standard emails' setting. The new `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` takes no metadata parameter and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members, and all attendees. Organizers who explicitly disabled standard emails for the event type will still receive these guest-added emails, breaking the documented email-suppression contract.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before the calendar update, leaving unrecoverable partial state on failure
findings.body: The handler writes the new guest rows with `prisma.booking.update` (line 92) and only afterwards calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165) outside any error handling. If the calendar update throws (e.g. expired OAuth token, as in the previous finding where the wrong user's credentials are used), the tRPC mutation returns an error, but the guests are already persisted in the database. When the user retries with the same emails, `uniqueGuests` becomes empty and they get the misleading `emails_must_be_unique_valid` BAD_REQUEST error, so they cannot recover without changing emails. The DB write and calendar update should be ordered/handled so a calendar failure doesn't strand a half-applied change (e.g. wrap the calendar update in try/catch like the email send, or roll back).

findings.title: Email send failure is swallowed with a console.log that drops the error object
findings.body: The catch block around `sendAddGuestsEmails` only prints the fixed string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and discards `err`, so there is no way to diagnose why emails failed (bad mail transport config, template error, etc.). Unlike a UI issue, this is a server-side silent failure with no log entry containing the actual error. Log the error (preferably via the app's logger) and include the error message/stack.

findings.title: Guests array has no min/max constraints
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts an empty array and an arbitrarily large one. An empty array is not rejected by the schema and instead surfaces later as the misleading `emails_must_be_unique_valid` BAD_REQUEST error, while an unbounded array lets one request create hundreds of attendee rows and trigger hundreds of outbound emails (each existing attendee gets an email per call), which is an email-bombing / resource-exhaustion vector even for an authenticated attendee. Add `.min(1)` and a sensible `.max(...)` (e.g. 10, matching the booking page guest limits).

findings.title: Invalid-email error is never cleared when the user corrects the input
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails, but it is only reset by the Cancel button or a successful mutation; it is never cleared when the user edits the email fields. After one failed attempt, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning stays displayed even while the user types valid emails, and remains visible during the subsequent in-flight mutation. Reset `isInvalidEmail` in the `MultiEmail` onChange path (or at the start of `handleAdd`).
